'''Justin Gregg''' is a Canadian science writer and professor of biology at [[St. Francis Xavier University]] in Nova Scotia, specializing in dolphin cognition.

==Biography==
Gregg's research is focused on the study of dolphin cognition. He received his [[PhD]] from the School of Psychology at [[Trinity College Dublin]] in 2008, going on to hold positions at the Dolphin Communication Project as a senior research associate and [[St. Francis Xavier University]] as an adjunct professor of biology.<ref>{{cite web |title=Justin Gregg |url=https://writers.ns.ca/member/justin-gregg/ |location=Halifax, N.S. |publisher=[[Writers' Federation of Nova Scotia]] |access-date=19 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Justin Gregg, Ph.D. |url=https://www.dolphincommunicationproject.org/justin-gregg/ |publisher=Dolphin Communication Project |access-date=19 December 2025}}</ref>

He is the author of three books. His 2022 book ''If Nietzsche Were a Narwhal'' was particularly well received, being variously described as "brilliant" and "compelling".<ref>{{cite web |author=((StFX)) |author-mask=[StFX] |date=6 February 2023 |title=International accolades continue for StFX professor Dr. Justin Gregg's book |url=https://www.stfx.ca/news/brilliant-compelling-first-rate-international-accolades-continue-stfx-professor-dr-justin |publisher=[[St. Francis Xavier University]] |access-date=19 December 2025}}</ref>

Beyond his academic work, Gregg has also produced and hosted podcasts, produced radio plays, and released albums with the children's musical group Bingly and the Rogues. He has done voice acting for animated films, and is the frontman for a punk rock band.<ref>{{cite web |last=Gregg |first=Justin |date=2025 |title=Meet Justin |url=https://www.justingregg.com/meetjustin |website=justingregg.com |access-date=19 December 2025}}</ref>
